newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says no low-sulphur diesel waivers yet sought.
newsitem.headline: EU says no low-sulphur diesel waivers yet sought.

text.p: The European Commission has received no requests from EU governments for waivers to an October 1 deadline for introducing new, lower-sulphur content diesel, an official told Reuters on Monday.
"At the present time, the Commission has not received any specific request from any country in relation to the directive," the official said.
From October 1, the maximum permitted sulphur content of diesel will be cut to 0.05 percent from 0.2 percent, in line with a 1993 EU directive.
The directive foresees a limited derogation allowing Greece to produce a higher sulphur content in diesel for marine use but for no other reason, the official said.
"The directive does not allow for any country to request a derogation for the deadlines," the official added.
Greece and Portugal were nevertheless reported on Friday to be seeking derogations.
